summary:

title: Vietnam attracts registered FDI worth $34.6 bn in H1 2026
summary:
Vietnam attracted registered FDI worth $34.6 billion in H1 2026—up by 61 per cent YoY. 
Disbursed FDI capital totalled $13.03 billion—up by 11.2 per cent. 
Newly-registered capital surged by 87.2 per cent, while capital contributions and share purchases rose by 89.5 per cent. 
Additional investment in existing projects rose by 23.5 per cent YoY, while manufacturing and processing was the largest recipient.

title: EU, G77, China reaffirm support for Bangladesh's LDC graduation
summary:
The EU and the Group of 77 and China recently reaffirmed their support for Bangladesh's efforts to ensure a smooth, sustainable and irreversible graduation from the LDC status.
The assurances came during meetings at the UN headquarters during the visit of Commerce Minister Khandakar Abdul Muktadir, who explained the logic behind the request for a three-year extension of the graduation preparatory period.

title: UK economy posts modest growth in May on stronger retail sales
summary:
UK output eked out modest growth in May, with a pre-summer heatwave supporting retail sales and probably other consumer-facing sectors.
CBI said the wider sector picture stayed mixed, keeping sustained momentum difficult for businesses.
Policy uncertainty, the Autumn Budget and energy-market volatility may weigh on confidence, investment and retail-linked supply chains.

title: Bangladesh’s $7.3 bn MMF boom has a 90% supply problem
summary:
Bangladesh exported $7.33 billion of selected MMF apparel in 2025, but imported $3.07 billion of MMF inputs, with China, India and Taiwan supplying 90.0 per cent. 
Woven fabrics accounted for 66.1 per cent of imports, highlighting reliance on upstream textile imports. 
Future competitiveness depends on expanding domestic yarn, fabric and finishing capabilities.

title: Ghana to revive Volta Star Textiles with strategic investor
summary:
Ghana has selected an investor to revive Volta Star Textiles, a defunct Juapong plant known for grey baft.
The project aims to restore production, create youth jobs and support secondary businesses in North Tongu.
Cotton will first come from Benin, while the plant is expected to offer farmers a guaranteed market.
The investor will inspect the site and finalise machinery retooling and refurbishment

title: US' producer price index falls 0.3% in June as goods prices decline
summary:
US' producer price index (PPI) for final demand fell 0.3 per cent in June as a 1.4 per cent drop in goods outweighed higher services.
Sourcing teams saw easing in input-linked areas, with lower energy, fuel, thermoplastic resin, raw cotton and processed intermediate goods.
Retail and service margins were firmer, including apparel, jewellery, footwear and accessories retailing, leaving cost signals mixed.

title: US small business confidence holds steady in Q2 2026
summary:
US small business confidence was broadly unchanged in Q2 2026, with the index at 66.5 against 67.0 in Q1 and 65.2 a year earlier.
Inflation is now the top concern for 57 per cent of owners, while local economy optimism fell to 33 per cent from 41 per cent.
Revenue and hiring expectations improved, but investment plans remain subdued, a signal for suppliers serving US small businesses.

title: Vietnam wage body agrees to 7.8% average hike in regional minimum wage
summary:

The wage will now rise by between 310,000 VND (~$11.81) and 390,000 VND per month, depending on the region. 
The proposal will be submitted to the government for approval.

title: Greece's apparel imports up 9.4% in Q1, led by cotton garments
summary:

Spain remained the largest supplier, followed by Italy and Germany, while cotton apparel accounted for 46.58 per cent of total imports.
Greece's apparel imports have grown steadily, reaching $2.72 billion in 2025.

title: EU bans destruction of unsold clothes, footwear from July 19
summary:
From July 19, large EU companies cannot destroy unsold clothes, clothing accessories and footwear under ESPR rules.
Medium-sized firms will face the same obligations from 2030, while small and micro-businesses are exempt.
Brands, retailers and suppliers must prioritise resale, donation, repair or reuse, with records kept for five years for inspections.

title: Morocco’s $3.94 bn apparel boom hides a $900 mn textile gap
summary:

Heavy reliance on imported materials and CMT manufacturing limits value capture. 
Future competitiveness will depend on integrated production, traceability, recycled materials and full-package manufacturing.

title: Bharat Tex 2026 backs global growth for Indian apparel brands
summary:
Indian textile and apparel brands discussed international scaling at Bharat Tex 2026, with export performance and 2030 targets framing the opportunity.
The session focused on converting manufacturing strength into design-led, culturally distinctive retail growth. 
Quality, sustainability, traceability, craft heritage and omnichannel reach emerged as priorities for global competitiveness.

title: UK's clothing imports drop 9.3% YoY in May 2026
summary:
The UK's clothing imports fell 9.3 per cent year on year to £1.301 billion (~$1.760 billion) in May 2026 and were 4.3 per cent lower than April, while textile fabric imports declined 2.8 per cent annually.
In Q1 2026, clothing imports eased 3.04 per cent year on year.
Despite the slowdown, the UK's clothing imports rose 6.05 per cent to £17.729 billion in 2025.

title: July's triple compliance shock hits apparel importers
summary:
CPSC eFiling adds an average $1,104 first-year compliance cost, affecting 43,000+ firms and 211,000+ children's product importers. 
The end of de minimis and USPS fees of up to $50 per non-compliant parcel raise fixed costs for low-value apparel shipments. 
Three July policy changes favour larger brands, widening their cost and operational advantage over smaller importers.

title: DGFT unveils Brand India initiative, T&A among priority sectors
summary:

The initiative proposes a Unified Brand India framework, a voluntary Trust Mark, branding support, and funding of up to ₹10 crore per project, with stakeholder consultations open for 30 days.

title: Cambodia's H1 2026 apparel exports up 5.7%; cotton imports surge
summary:

title: Bangladesh’s EU export decline points to a shift in apparel sourcing
summary:
BKMEA says H&M’s Bangladesh orders are ~40 per cent lower YoY, while FY26 apparel exports fell 1.64 per cent, led by a 3.31 per cent drop in EU shipments. 
Germany’s imports from Bangladesh fell 11.5 per cent ($570 million), driving most of the country’s $645 million export decline. 
India gains with UK tariff-free access, a pending EU FTA, and ₹95,000 crore in planned textile investments.

title: Africa’s apparel exporters have less than six months of certainty
summary:
Africa’s apparel exports reached $8.62 billion in 2025, but AGOA’s expiry in 170 days is limiting long-term investment despite supporting current orders.
